newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - April 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - April 23.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.
- A close friend of Kim Hyun-chul, the second son of President Kim Young-sam, denied on Tuesday, any connection with the failed Hanbo Group or his is role as the manager of Hyun-chul's properties.
- North and South Korea have decided to co-develop an industrial estate in the Rajin-Sunbong free-trade zone in North Korea, the Korea Land Corporation said.

- Debt-stricken Jinro Group just barely avoided insolvency thanks to its creditor banks' rescue measures, and its chairman, Chang Jin-ho, plans to give up management rights for several affilates of Jinro.
- May 18, the anniversary of the 1980 Kwangju massacre, will be designated as a "legal commemoration day" the government announced Tuesday.
- Talks to persuade North Korea to join peace negotiations broke down after the United States and South Korea refused the North's demand for additional food aid.
- North Korea on Tuesday called defector Hwnag Jang-yop a "cowardly traitor" in its first reaction to hwang's dramatic entry into South Korea on Sunday.
- Hwang Jang-yop, the highest-level North Korean official to defect to South Korea, warned that the North can turn the South into a "sea of fire" with its nuclear and chemical weapons.

- Related government authorities will investigate the "North Korean underground organizations" in South Korea which North Korean defector Hwang Jang-yop mentioned in a paper he wrote last August, a government offical said on Tuesday.
